title: Load-Bearing Gap Summary

canonical_node.axiom: The 10-variable product form is either derivable from the chi-field Lagrangian or must be explicitly treated as a postulate/axiom in the Lean layer and in public claims.
definitions: chi-field Lagrangian: the formal Lagrangian defining the chi-field, whose exact definition is to be located.
10-variable product form: the product form involving 10 variables, whose exact definition is to be located.
bridge: a formal derivation connecting the chi-field Lagrangian to the 10-variable product form.
derivation: The document identifies the Lagrangian-to-product-form bridge as the central formal gap.
It states that downstream claims depend on the product form as a load-bearing spine.
It asserts that if the product form is derived, the system is stronger; if assumed, public wording must change.
It lists professional tasks to locate definitions and determine the status of the product form.
canonical_node.action: Determine whether the 10-variable product form is derivable from the chi-field Lagrangian; if derivable, formalize the bridge in Lean; if not, add explicit axiom/postulate labels and revise public claim status.
boundary: This document does not itself provide the derivation or the formal definitions.
It does not assert that the product form is derivable or not; it only identifies the gap and required actions.
It does not resolve secondary gaps such as marker theorems or provenance.
test: Check whether a formal Lean proof exists that derives the 10-variable product form from the chi-field Lagrangian.
Check whether the product form is explicitly labeled as an axiom/postulate in the Lean layer and public claims if not derived.
Check whether public claims are revised to match the actual formal status.

dg1_dependencies: Exact formal definition of the chi-field Lagrangian
Exact formal definition of the 10-variable product form
Lean formalization of the bridge if derivable
dg_protocol.dg2_new_capability: Provides a clear directive to close the central formal gap by either deriving the product form or explicitly labeling it as an axiom, thereby enabling honest and accurate public claims.
dg_protocol.dg3_preserved_floor: Preserves the existing conditional/postulated status of the product form as recorded in the V2 ledger, and maintains the requirement for honest public wording.
dg_protocol.dg4_collapse_if_removed: If this node is removed, the framework loses the explicit identification of the central gap and the directive to resolve it, risking continued overstatement in public claims.
dg5_translation_registers: Lean formal proof of the bridge

classification.recommended_atom_action: track as a task/requirement; do not treat as a proven theorem

overstatement_risks: Treating the product form as derived without a formal proof
Public claims exceeding the formal status of the product form
Ignoring the need to label the product form as an axiom if not derived
kill_conditions: If the bridge is proven derivable, the axiom label is unnecessary; the node's directive becomes obsolete.
If the bridge is proven not derivable and the product form is not labeled as an axiom, the node's directive is violated.
risk.lean_target: Formalize the bridge in Lean if derivable; otherwise, add axiom/postulate labels to the product form in the Lean layer.

plain_summary: This document identifies the main formal gap: whether the 10-variable product form can be derived from the chi-field Lagrangian. It says that if it can be derived, the system is stronger; if not, it must be treated as an axiom and public claims must be adjusted. The document does not itself provide the derivation or definitions, so it is a directive for future work, not a proof.
